[Date]

Molina Healthcare  
Attn: Appeals and Grievances Department  
[Appeals mailing address, fax number, or electronic submission location confirmed by Molina]

Re: Internal appeal of denial of rotator cuff repair  
Member: Cameron Grant  
Member ID: W314904804  
Reference number: POC-9DD444765E-23652  
Requested service: Arthroscopic rotator cuff repair  
CPT: 29827  
Denial notice date: August 8, 2026

Dear Molina Appeals Reviewer:

I appeal Molina’s denial of prior authorization for CPT 29827, arthroscopic rotator cuff repair. The denial states that the procedure does not meet the plan’s medical-necessity criteria. I request that Molina overturn the denial and authorize the requested surgery.

The clinical record supports medical necessity:

- I have had 24 months of progressive shoulder pain that has not resolved with rest.
- I completed 20 supervised physical-therapy visits over eight weeks, from May 20, 2026, through July 15, 2026. Therapy focused on rotator-cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics. The physical-therapy discharge note documents this treatment.
- I used NSAIDs for eight months with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on June 8, 2026, produced only four weeks of partial relief.
- MRI on June 5, 2026, showed a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm, with grade 2 fatty atrophy.
- I cannot lift the affected arm above shoulder height and cannot sleep on the affected side.
- Examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.
- There is no active infection or untreated substance-use condition. My BMI is 29, and I am a nonsmoker.
- The treating surgeon, Okafor, MD, is an orthopedic surgeon.

These records demonstrate a structural full-thickness rotator-cuff tear, persistent symptoms and functional impairment, failure of substantial conservative treatment, and inadequate response to medication and injection therapy. They also identify no documented clinical contraindication to the requested procedure.

The plan has not provided the specific medical-necessity policy or clinical-review criteria used for this denial, and I was unable to verify a publicly available Arizona Commercial/ACA policy governing CPT 29827. Therefore, this appeal does not quote or assume any plan policy language. Please identify the exact policy or clinical criteria applied to this request, including the title, policy number, version, effective date, and specific criteria on which Molina relied. Please also provide the clinical rationale and all records considered in making the denial.

If Molina believes additional information is required, please identify each missing item and give the treating physician an opportunity to provide it. Please have the request reviewed by an appropriately qualified orthopedic physician who was not involved in the original denial.

Please reverse the adverse determination and approve CPT 29827. If Molina upholds the denial, please provide a written explanation addressing each clinical fact above, the exact criteria applied, the evidence supporting the decision, and all further appeal and external-review rights.

This appeal must be received by February 4, 2027. Please send written confirmation of receipt and the appeal determination to me at:

Cameron Grant  
[Mailing address]  
[Telephone number]  
[Email address]

Sincerely,

Cameron Grant  
Member ID: W314904804
